An interstellar cruise ship offers tours to exotic planets, including one where the owner apparently cares about little else but space: a review of Marzamini: An Interstellar Adventure by Eric Willeman, from The Millennium Review.
Marzamini is the outlandish title for a fantasy novel by Eric Willeman. The character of this book is completely different from any conceivable representation of a future astronaut in a century’s time. Will, the hero, is a dreamer who can see into the future. He is not the sort of character who has to fit into society, or with whom one can identify. He has nothing but romance and astrophotography as interests and hobbies, and has zero desire to travel to far-off worlds, even though he plans to live there.
I will confess that this is a book that I have not read. I have never gone into one of Willeman’s previous books, since I’m not a fan of fantasy or science fiction. But I had heard great things about this particular book. In fact, my general fascination with romance seems to have intensified with the publication of it. The fact that Eric Willeman has cast the hero as the love interest for the heroine has rung true for me, because I’ve recently become obsessed with little-known historical female astronauts. I am fascinated by them, because they appear to have been notorious as romantic heroines, and I think their stories deserve their popularity.
Eric Willeman, the writer of Marzamini: An Interstellar Adventure, is an underappreciated writer. He’s a relatively obscure author of children’s literature, so most of the books I’ve come across don’t get my attention. But I was completely beguiled by Marzamini: An Interstellar Adventure. It is a fantastic, dreamlike romance novel that evokes the imagery of Jules Verne’s Jules Verne’s Journey to the Center of the Earth.
I guess I always knew Willy wasn’t an astronaut. He lived like a normal old guy who worked at a dry cleaner in little Tokyo. But what I didn’t realize was that Willy and his palki weren’t astronauts. They were amateurs trying to impress their girlfriends with astrophotography skills. What was so special about that? It seemed the art of celestial photography was a complete secret that Willy had never heard about. But he went hunting for it anyway.
And I can tell you that, if you know Willy, he’s a lover of space. He’s a guy who comes up with great excuses to get to the planet, or at least to a planetary-like structure that looks just like one of Willy’s apartment buildings. He’s just a guy with his camera in hand and a big imagination. But he’s no real astronaut. He doesn’t eat nothing but shakshuka for lunch, and he spends more time watching TV shows about astronauts than he does looking for comets in the sky. He also has no desire to ever explore other planets. But it’s just so romantic to see him trying to do what everyone else does.
It’s almost a luridly cheesy novel, with Willy and his palki taking turns looking up at a comet or something with the help of telescopes that are near their apartment complex. He always comes away with some great photos of comets, and I think that this may have been how Jules de Verne’s character chose to memorialize his journeys to the stars.
The story, a romance novel with elements of a time-traveling romance, features a girl who, in a touching moment, gently tugs the reader’s heartstrings away from the escapism of Willy and his palki. It has a touching ending. Will has to give up his dream of a romantic relationship to finish his work and settle down. But this isn’t a happy, cliched conclusion. He is in fact devastated to return home after discovering that his time has run out.
It’s clear that Willy is not an astronaut. He’s an amateur astrophotographer who dreams of exploring space himself. But I have to say that I was a little disappointed that this ending wasn’t exactly what I expected it to be. He probably realizes that he’s going to die now, since he has an urgent obligation to try to find a suitable girlfriend, and maybe even build a new one in the process. But it’s a kind of tearfully bittersweet farewell to a possible romance.
The location of Willy’s apartment building, clearly modeled after a quaint little apartment building that he runs into, while back in the real world.
Maybe it’s possible to imagine what a spaceship might look like, but I personally never saw one like Willy’s.
The back cover says it all: “This is a time-travel romance.” So what is the significance of Willy wearing eyeglasses? It’s actually quite important, because there is a little extra dimension to Willy’s personality.
Eric Willeman is a great writer, so I’m not going to repeat everything that I’ve just said about this novel in order to spoil it for you. But I encourage you to check it out. It’s not a particularly deep read, but it’s a far more imaginative read than some of my favorite kinds of novel: fantasy novels about the dangers of alien contact or science-fiction with a social/political message.
But if you’re a romance fan, you probably want to read it. Marzamini has a fantastic end. It’s not the best kind of fantasy, but the best kinds of fantasy don’t have a happy ending.

The craftsmanship of ancient pottery tells a story of cultural heritage and is as exciting as it is aesthetic. There are now very few pieces remaining of the traditional style of Early Mesopotamian pottery, but this category is still represented in the market. In fact, in the modern form of art ceramics, a new world of imaginative and complex work is created by arranging hundreds of layers of decorative colors in a mathematical pattern.
Thus, this design is the result of the perfect harmony of the forces of nature and man. The production of the pieces of these pottery is a ritual that takes many hours of working on an immovable territory in the open air, transforming the dust, the fire and the earth into a soft ceramic.

The night following the tragic death of his father, Jason Hammond, Jovan went out looking for a place to stay and found his first true home at Canyon Hospice & Home.
Since then, the youngster has become a vital member of the community, serving as an inspiration to others and a beacon of hope.

One of the most heartwarming stories of the year so far, with staff at Canyon Hospice supporting Jovan’s transition from the homeless into a role in the community, has seen unprecedented support for Canyon’s Street Santa Service over the past 12 months.
Street Santa Service began in 2016 in an effort to encourage and provide a positive impact on lives touched by the tragedy of homelessness. The service is always open to anyone looking for a reason to be cheerful.
Street Santa is an activity which gives a range of staff members the opportunity to meet and interact with their clients in a calm, no pressure environment, where they can listen to them and provide information in an efficient and respectful manner.
The service also supports people in a positive way, to ensure they feel better and more relaxed during the whole process, where they’re supported in getting advice on changes to their circumstances and the provision of support.
On Christmas day 2016, the Service was able to support 14 people in giving a 26-year-old female a Christmas gift.
Street Santa also delivered Christmas presents to 20 homeless children in the December months of 2017. Each child received a gift box filled with goodies like packs of bread, chocolate, toothpaste and children’s books, as well as socks, gloves and glove boots.
All the gifts were delivered by Canyon’s own Street Santa team, the nail art was painted by Street Artist, volunteer art teacher Brent Everett.

For the whole team at Canyon, the response to Street Santa over the last 12 months has been enormous.
To know that Jovan, who has had his own fair share of struggles, has been recognised for his contribution to our community in a way that we’re proud to support is truly inspirational.
It's been an amazing year for the Canyon team, as we’ve seen a massive jump in attendance and, ultimately, more of our clients coming through our doors to visit us.

The master potter's hands shaped the clay into a work of art, decorating it with simple, delicate line work and bright hues. The markings on the clay express a woman’s characteristics, and in turn the carving reveals the artist’s creative technique.
With tradition, an ancestor’s memories or a craftsman’s ambition, an exchange of everyday life and modern life merge to create clay sculptures that engage with people’s lives and help them express themselves.
Ceramic clay is one of the most common forms of medium used in ceramic art. The basic elements are formed and condensed under special conditions, giving a glossy surface finish. Clay may be made from a powdered clay that has been dry ground and kept in a container that is filled with water and then kneaded. The clay may be made from a base material called a "slip", and this is turned into a substance that is dried and compressed by heating. This process leaves bare clay "raw". A clay will give back all of the water. After the drying, the clay will be prepared for the act of firing. Most often, a liquid fire is used to heat the clay body to the point where it is ready for glazing.
A panel of our glaze is composed of a range of colours. It is also possible to add "extras" like hand painted decorations, coloured glazes or patches of a kiln interior, which adds to the richness of each piece.
Beatrice describes her clay pieces, often in the form of little flowers or leaves, as the clay “forms and molds into these forms. I add many decorative elements and also special white to draw attention to them, and they are often highlighted. They make my work more complete”.
Beatrice’s work has been exhibited in the exhibitions at the German Ceramic Association as well as the exhibition “Kunst und Kugeln” in the Salon 5 at the German State of Saxony in Frankfort and the Euro-Bodense Museum in Schwenningen (from 28th of January to 13th of April 2009).

The serene landscape of the countryside was dotted with spots of delightful and attractive shops. After passing through the twin villages of Chenean-la-Arriere and Chenean-sur-Seul, we arrived at the site of our first stay – the Lunay Castle. This is where we first got the idea for the tour of Lunay; an exquisite property full of history that was built in the XVI century by one of the most renowned and illustrious French artists of the period, Jean Baptiste-Joseph Baumay.
From the castle, we drove through the heart of Arudes, just the opposite of Lunay, to visit Lunay Manor. The property consists of a manor house, a beautiful temple, as well as a walled garden with an archery court. The castle was built by Jean Baptiste-Joseph Baumay in 1605; he had this property built in the middle of a moated estate, in the heart of one of the foremost duchy of Languedoc. Originally he built a new castle for his son and grew a tree of immense splendor. In this site, Baumay also designed the Temple of Saint Ardent. The temple is situated in the middle of a pond, alongside the grotto, the Orangery and the Tunnel of Love.
In the outdoor park, a massive square is surrounded by 200 roses, as well as statues and a flower bed. The atmosphere is slightly more relaxed at this more intimate square. During our stay, we wandered through the park, while the children enjoyed themselves at the toy truck.
Next stop: Val-Jourdain (Palu). During the Renaissance, Val-Jourdain had the advantage of being the strongest city in the region. The first settlements date back to 550 BC, and it became an important trading centre. It was a stronghold of the Languedoc Kingdom during the 11th century.
Located next to Orangery, the Fortress, we drove into this fortified outpost. Built in the XIV century, its arches are round and its interior features some beautiful staircases. The prison had the role of keeping the English prisoners in the castle and, most importantly, of holding the commander for being one of the 4 main pillars of the Languedoc Crusades.
After a short break, we stopped at the Hotel des Pats. It is set around a large pond, surrounded by fountains and shrubs. There is a small swimming pool, perfect for relaxing in the sun with a good book. For the kids, there is a funfair with pendulums, a sailing boat, a paddling pool and a large trampoline.
During our tour, we visited the Poor House and the two orphanages, including the home for widows and small children. This allows us to go back into our stay at the Manor.
Later on in the day, we had a visit to Lunay Castle. From there we drove back through the valley to Lunay and Les Plages.
Then it was time to make our way back to Arudes.
Thank you to the Lunay Manor, and our numerous tour guides, who were always helpful and keen to make our stay in Lunay as memorable as possible. We highly recommend a stay in Lunay to all our guests who want to see more of the south of France.

In a world where books can alter reality, a forgotten tome in an old bookstore can hold all the answers. No matter how you dive into a historical text, there are some things you can never grasp without an "unsurprising" guidebook, a handy guide to the history of a single topic. And whatever the title may be, there's nothing more confusing than digging through old tomes in need of translating, only to find them poorly dressed and unreadable in a dank, dark corner. But in the 1980s, this very problem plagued a local college library when it was taken over by a dedicated librarian and expanded collection from the lands it once held. Lined with old, ignored tomes in need of a new chapter? The librarian of the past that you seek is in the attic. He's been there for years, and he knows the history of the topics in every single book. This "How to" Manual for researchers, students, and curious historians allows them to take on the books within the library itself, getting an unsurpassed degree of access that no subject or research can match.
Human curiosity is something that drives stories, and when interest is sparked with something new, it's impossible not to pick up a book and read. The thirst for knowledge and artistic development that caused the stories that have formed this world and shaped its history are always filled with interesting topics and worlds. This book offers the reader a simple understanding of how to source what a historian needs, and how to pick up books that are hidden beneath old overstuffed tomes in a library, enabling the reader to find the true story of their source material. It is for those readers who don't get the background on how certain parts of history get lost or forgotten, and for those readers who just need to learn more about history and the places they've read about. The text, called Mukhyamitra, has 1308 chapters on dreams and is sometimes referred to as the 'Tiger of Dreams'.
The text, which is the most important manuscript in the world, has been printed in Nepal for the first time in 25 years.
It was brought to Bhaktapur on Sunday by Sanjai Thapa, 56, editor of Dharmicari, the oldest Nepali classical bookshop, which has had the book for nearly 30 years.
Sangeeta Karki, 52, who also has her own company called Karki Printing, told BBC Television's Newsnight that the text, once called the Rukmasmaya, had changed in its origins but the narrative had remained the same.

Wolf, the namesake of the U.S. Nuclear Deterrent Treaty, is in the desert of Western Nevada. She stands guard over the likely deaths of many thousands of wolves as they leap from the sand-dunes.
Wolf Conservation Trust (WCT) is the only non-profit dedicated to the conservation of America’s wolves and their habitats. The WCT partners with various resource agencies in the West and makes programs to protect and educate people and wildlife.
At their annual meeting in April, the Western Slope Range Wolves Conservation Board will determine whether or not to designate Wolf Conservation Trust as a non-profit for tax-exempt status.
Wolf Conservation Trust has been working with landowners in this region for over 25 years. The livestock owners have, or should, have decisions they must make as to how to use their grazing land. The policy of the Western Slope Range Wolves Conservation Board is to “educate the landowners” about the value of the grazing land on their lands. Wolf Conservation Trust has done this for the past 25 years. In that time, WCT has helped to educate more than 35,000 livestock owners about the value of their lands.
In November of 2006, Wolf Conservation Trust merged with the Paiute Tribe to form the WCT. WCT continues to serve as a subsidiary of the Paiute Tribe. However, it is now a separate legal entity that has all of the assets of a corporation and is governed by a board of directors and by the By-Laws of the Incorporated Organization.
The Paiute Tribe is the only tribe to form a non-profit corporation within the 160 miles of the Silver State’s border and made its firsts move into that territory in 1953. The Paiute Tribe’s mission is to preserve its culture and continue the preservation of its history.
The Paiute have always had a strong sense of self. Most people are more concerned about protecting their individual cultural heritage and we consider the fact that we are the only tribe that can govern ourselves to be a blessing. The Paiutes have always been independent and proud. It was a matter of time before they became more involved in the WCT program.
The Western Slope Range Wolves Conservation Board is comprised of 15 representatives from various government agencies and the Paiute Tribe. The group meets four times a year. Each time they meet they discuss the local needs of the region. These meetings are for the benefit of the WCT and the other non-profits that Wolf Conservation Trust is working with in the West. The board members are very busy during these meetings. We will be meeting on November 12th to consider adopting a special rule to allow WCT to begin building up its bank account to do more things. The board is also considering a rule to allow us to expand our programs.
This will mean a whole new approach to projects. Now, we are going to be thinking about doing things differently. Now we will be thinking about how to partner with landowners. These meetings are going to increase our success and ability to do things that we would not be able to do without the involvement of the various resource agencies.
The board does not even have to vote on these new rules to come up with them. That is the reason for having a quorum. I also have a number of additional things that I need to do that are not part of the formal meetings.
Wolf Conservation Trust is only in the business of working with landowners. We can’t take on government responsibilities and have a successful non-profit organization. They are already successful, but they are not fully involved with ranchers in the West because it is very difficult to find a way for these various entities to come together.
Some ranchers have been extremely supportive. They have had a number of meetings with us and the idea of partnering together has been very appealing to them. There has been a lot of discussion about this.
The Paiute Tribe had the idea of bringing in a group to look at this from an animal management standpoint. We had the group think about wildlife issues from an economic perspective.
Because of the idea of partnering with other agencies, the Wildlife Services, the Bureau of Land Management, Fish and Wildlife Service, etc., our community has had very little exposure to the job of preventing the loss of wildlife on federal lands.
The state game warden came up with the idea of having wildlife management as part of our board membership. The Wildlife Services is really our first friend. They provided us with a parcel of land for 16 years to do our habitat management work on. This is where we have learned about endangered species and have learned how to build strong wildlife networks. That parcel of land is a perfect example of what can be done to change the situation for the benefit of wildlife and for the public.
We also want to work with the Paiute Tribe. I will also be looking at the partnership with the BLM as we look at how to manage the wolf. My feeling is that it would be very beneficial to us to partner with BLM on the wolf management on this particular tract of land. I will see how far we are going to go before we reach that decision.
It is important for us to move forward to look at funding our projects. We need to figure out a way to raise money. We had the idea of putting together a sales tax thing because we were always charging people to do the things we did. The WCT board always looked for ways to raise money to help us.
Our goal is to make our program more focused on creating more jobs in the region. We want to make the point to the ranchers that we are not only a good thing for ranchers but that this is going to be a good thing for the ranchers. We will continue to work with landowners as we expand and grow the programs.
If you have an idea, I want to hear about it. I will keep you informed as we progress. The board meetings are on the third Thursday of each month. We meet at Wolf Management Center. The board members may attend, but it is more beneficial for you to make a visit. We have monthly slides from one of the projects we have done and monthly slides from the next project that will be going on.

Reviewed by Mark Luttrell
It’s A Wonderful Ghost Story
It’s a story that every friend is going to think of as they pore over the various metaphors to describe the strange events taking place in this small New England town. Like the object of the story’s antagonist, Vera, the ghost is also a woman. The owner of an antique store in town, Vera enjoys the remembrance of her late husband. Her flamboyant persona and impeccable humor are somewhat endearing, yet few, perhaps, do not begin to understand why she’s not to be trusted.
All of the town’s residents know this because Vera is the target of certain afflictions. These afflictions are quickly and tragically resolved; however, it doesn’t appear that she has a natural gift for fighting back. In some cases, the mundane is not enough to resolve the situation, causing Vera to opt to amass a very large collection of otherworldly items. It isn’t until she teams up with the local witch and the enigmatic town counselor that her haunting, nightmarish experiences come to a definite end.
Directed by Blair Friedlander, it’s a “throwback” kind of film that draws its appeal from the fact that it’s a ghost story in the very traditional sense. One element that sets this film apart from the crowd is that it doesn’t just rely on telling an interesting story about Vera and her decisions as a headstrong, single woman; it does so in ways that allow the protagonist to demonstrate her psychological battle with demons of her own creation.
Because Vera is so strong willed and accomplished in the beginning, it isn’t long before her behavior seems out of character. Her relationship with a little girl, Judy, begins to suffer because the child begins to react emotionally to Vera’s presence. There’s also a lot of similarities to the Burkes and Hitchcock films in terms of its own tone. The setup to the film is classic, while the outcomes are not. It’s a well-constructed film that takes time to get to where it is, and the performances are superb throughout.
If you’re looking for a ghost story, I highly recommend At the Annual Ghost Convention. The lack of dialogue in some scenes, and the scene where Vera wanders the church grounds in her encounter with one of the spooks in black garb are two of the highlights of the film. I was surprised by the quality of the filming in regards to the couple of sets that were used. One small addition that would have benefitted the film is a scene where Vera is walking down the main street in the rain, only to come face to face with a young child. Instead, she runs into another character from the story, but there are no witnesses to this event in the film. It just wouldn’t make sense to have multiple versions of a single occurrence.
At the Annual Ghost Convention is a well-executed story that fits with a well-executed genre that is never afraid to give the audience a good dose of entertainment. At the same time, it’s never too sentimental or sentimentalized in any way.

In Case You Missed It
The Rams were the most successful franchise in the NFC last season, finishing with a record of 13-3. They had never made the playoffs since the inception of the Super Bowl, and all but won the first Super Bowl they had never won before, which was against the Saints. What made them so successful that year? A few things. The team was young, led by quarterback Jared Goff, who was only 24 years old. The Rams had a rookie running back named Todd Gurley, who played all year and was considered by many to be the best rookie quarterback in the NFL. The Rams had plenty of weapons on offense, which included receivers Brandin Cooks and Kendall Hunter, and defensive standouts Von Miller and Nick Foles. Foles was so good that he was given a no-pass-rush tag, and allowed to throw right into his running backs for jump starts, which added to their overall effectiveness.
The Rams got off to a slow start, and their third quarterback, Kurt Warner, had to be replaced by Cam Newton. They finished the season with a record of 6-13, but that season was considered by many to be the beginning of the end for the Rams. After that loss to the Saints, they decided to make some big changes to their organization, trading up in the draft to take QB Jared Goff and setting up a full off-season of change for their team. They traded up and took QB Andrew Luck from the Colts. The team still struggled, finishing the season at 3-14.
This season, the Rams had two changes that made the difference in their playoff run. They traded up in the draft to get WR Brandin Cooks. They also made a big change in their coaching staff, hiring Chip Kelly. These changes made them ready to make a deeper run, and could be considered the turning point of the season. As with any team with a new head coach, the changes in personnel add another layer of momentum to the team’s playoff run. With the big contracts they have, the Rams have a lot of money in their pockets, and they want to pay the players well. Goff is a second year quarterback, but Gurley is still young, and the rookies on the team have been efficient. This year they looked like a team that could compete with any team in the NFL, which was a big deal for fans. They finished the season at 11-4, which left them with a spot in the playoffs.
In a year when the Rams seemed to be heading in the right direction, the team made a major mistake that cost them a playoff spot. They traded a 5th round pick to the Cardinals for a 4th rounder. The Rams traded away a lot of good players and traded up to take a pick from the Cardinals for a 4th rounder. This was the one area where the team made a mistake, and it was really unforgivable. If they had just stuck with their original plan, they would have made it to the playoffs. They still managed to do the best they possibly could and ended up finishing the season with a record of 11-4, which was enough to take them to the playoffs. In a close game, they finished with a score of 30-28. They would have won the game and a chance to have the NFL’s best record, if they didn’t give up that 4th round pick.
There was a lot of change for the Rams this year. They traded up and took a 4th rounder to get a top 20 pick. They also made a trade to get the top 20 pick in the draft, which was good for them because they still have plenty of good players. They ended up finishing with a record of 11-4, which was good enough to be in the playoffs. This is a big change for the team, as it makes them the top team in the NFL and is one of the biggest reasons why they made it to the playoffs. They are still a team with a lot of weapons on offense, and they are a team with a lot of young players. They are a team that is very capable of doing a lot of good things in the NFL, and they have all of the pieces to be a very good team for a long time.

Beneath the surface of the calm lake lies the one area of the valley that is often turned into a nightmare for drivers – the narrow, twisting lane of dangerous Emergency Services. A narrow strip of road that no one wants to be driving on!
But with under 2 miles of road to walk to take you out of a tight spot and 2.1 miles of wide roads to get out, Emergency services have to be quick about their responses and that’s what the BHSSC is doing to help.
A new training course has been launched that will not only help them to be quicker and safer on emergency crews – it will also save a company money.
Established to help emergency services achieve this, the BHSSC are behind the specially designed course to teach them what to do when they are called out to a site.
The course focuses on three main areas of practice, the driver or driver-carer, the fire officer and the police.
It will cover the differences in how they see the area of the road where a crewed vehicle may be encountered, the effect of traffic on the driver’s personal space and car and the hazards that can arise in a tight spot.
“Talk to your colleagues about the training and hopefully they will be willing to help in some way,” says Louise McGuinness, head of education and development at the BHSSC.
“We have developed the course to ensure people are fully prepared, give sound advice and they are able to follow through.”
The training covers different weather conditions, evacuation, first aid and critical care.
The course is suitable for all crewed emergency services personnel including police, firefighters and ambulance service paramedics. It can also be taken by other emergency service crews who have been requested to attend.
The course is a three-day course and there are times to drop in or drop out as needed. It is not compulsory and everyone who attends is free to take it when they are able to.
“Taking on board your colleagues is a huge step for the BHSSC and with this course, we hope to give them confidence,” adds McGuinness.
The training is being rolled out over the next year to 500 members of the emergency services and after that to 1,000 further crews, ambulance crews, search and rescue and council units.
“The course is a great addition to what we already have and we feel it is a stepping stone to the future,” adds McGuinness.
“This will be the first of its kind in Scotland and it will hopefully give the information to help the public too.”
If you are interested in the course or have any questions about it, please get in touch with the BHSSC at info@bhsschildren.org.uk
The BHSSC is also in the process of setting up an online course to cover all the core skills and information people need in the emergency services to know. This will be available in spring 2019 and the cost will be negotiated with the provider, not be included in any training or assessment fees.

The decision to embark on a solo travel adventure leads to life-changing experiences in some surprising ways.
A mother of two from Hendersonville, TN, set off on a solo trip in July of 2008. It was her fourth solo trip.
“I was feeling good in the summer and over the summer it was a great time to take a vacation, but as you know, vacationing on your own can be stressful, and life can get in the way,” said Lynn.
But the vacation didn’t go the way she had planned. She had planned to spend three weeks relaxing in Cancun, Mexico, but ended up only being able to leave 24 hours later and return to the airport to spend the night.
On top of that, her daughter was starting preschool and she had been to the family doctor only once in her life.
“The doctor told me that as I would get older, I would get more frequent eye exams,” said Lynn.
She got the nod, but then realized she was staring at two years. She had to wait eight weeks, but they were woefully inadequate for a specialist’s exam and the eye doctor warned her it might take 18 months.
Hey, she was going to be 49 when she left. Just a bit too long.
Then, her sister was having a baby, and she had wanted to travel to Ireland, so she asked her to drive her to a nightclub. The mamacita was awesome, but she got back on the road to rebound with her vacation.
On the way home she realized she needed to get a rest. She found the RV at a stop light, and made an U-turn and went home, making sure to send a copy of her passport to the son she didn’t know.
Lynn had been to 10 different countries, so it didn’t take long for her husband to figure out that she was on her own again.
“I told him that when he got home he had to go and wake my up for a rest,” said Lynn.
Lynn has been asked many times by friends and family what she had gotten out of it.
She found it to be the best experience of her life, but even that was limited.
“I wasn’t as relaxed as I wanted to be because of the anticipation, and I was sitting around the whole time trying to get something to eat,” said Lynn.
At the end of the trip she had more than a whole year to live, but she realized it wasn’t too late to live the life she had always dreamed of.
“I thought I didn’t have much more time to live and I was so disappointed when I didn’t get to do all the things I wanted to do,” said Lynn.
Afterwards she was overcome with emotion and decided to put everything together and have a more traditional wedding. She had never been to a wedding, so she chose to pick out the flower for her own ceremony and had the reception at her own location.
“She really got to experience it the way she wanted it to be,” said Matt.
Lynn and her sister celebrated their birthdays with friends and family in November.
“I was able to get the dream of a lifetime, and it really does have made an impact on the way I look at things,” said Lynn.
Lynn believes her solo trip gave her some peace and solitude to think and to examine her life. Her next adventure will have to wait until she’s in her 50s, but that’s no matter.
“I think at 49 I would have done the same trip at 49,” said Lynn.

During the world's quietest concert, the audience realizes the music is not heard, but felt through the very sense of touch. With her first CD Elegant Imperfection, violinist Christine Perri found that this phenomenon (no pun intended) is universal and common to everyone.
The CD was recorded during the last months of 2005 and is a part of her latest endeavor: her second solo CD Thousands of Tiny Secrets, out in July 2007. The concept of the CD came from a recent conversation with a friend, who said, "I am a very small person and I play violin very small."
This was the basis of her answer when asked the age of her instruments: an 1810 Stradivarius violin. For the rest of the CD, the entire violin is played with just the right touch, rather than the full sound of the instrument.
The CD opens with "Suite No. 2" from the children's music collection "The Story of a Dog and a Rabbit" by Leo Dalour. The suitably acoustic sound is projected over a major work called "Suite No. 1" for violin and piano, by Dmitri Shostakovich. The suitably acoustic sound is projected over a major work called "Symphony No. 6" for violin and orchestra, by Shostakovich. The CD ends with two duets, by Zanele Muholi and Mireille Brugada, an altruistic combination of violinist and keyboardist.
Some say they are simply self-assured, others say that they are all self-assured. But this review does not deny their ability to be assured, although it certainly is obvious through this one. A 19th century violin of truly superb craftsmanship. The sound of the violin is truly amazing.
What the viola did not say was, at least in the CD's opening, how in a piece of music such as "Symphony No. 5" by the Albanian pianist she plays on the CD, the listener could not necessarily connect the two personalities of the violin and the piano player of the CD. Maybe the violin and piano player are so similar in their everyday, humdrum lives, that they do not interact in concert, that they are the same thing? Whatever the reason, in a piece such as the violin's muted double-stop, the violin was quite upstaged.
The Mireille Brugada and Zanele Muholi on this CD are such a team. Their collaboration is, in some ways, the complete opposite of what is actually happening in the recording: the sound of each of them is much more clearly heard. They were playing together, I thought, as if they were playing as a team. I guess you can say they were playing to themselves.
It's not always about teamwork. It's about being a player, who only wants to make sound. Well, it was actually that way when the two players were onstage, a couple of years ago. The CD was just released, and the premiere for the album and concerts was to take place a month or two later. And what happened? They just played the CD.
I don't think I've ever heard anything so closely synchronized by two players of the violin. I'd like to hear more of that, with the kind of music that makes violinists go to that place within themselves they rarely get to access. But at the risk of having to replay this piece of music a couple of times in my head before it could be enjoyed, I think you can thank the violinist for this. She won't be afraid of being the star, in a situation such as this one.
Some of these people, I mean. I had no idea. What I really wanted was to be the star. At least, this CD seemed to suggest it.

A mysterious artifact uncovered in Egypt revealed the start of an ancient civilization
A team from the American University in Cairo unearthed a mysterious tomb filled with astonishing findings. The artifacts and discoveries will help scientists understand the Egyptians and their ancestors.
Although the tomb has been investigated since the beginning of the year, the details on the state of the tomb, its deteriorated condition, and the whole tomb’s contents are still unclear.
A team of researchers, led by a group of scientists from the American University in Cairo, examined the tomb, located in Giza Plateau, outside the Egyptian capital. While the tomb is huge, its origins are still unknown. It is believed that the tomb was constructed sometime during the 15th century B.C.E.
The team discovered an ancient Egyptian tomb called a sepulchral complex. This tomb is large, but is believed to be built on a structure called the Amenhotep II resting place, which was once a royal family shrine to the mummies of the former pharaoh.
Experts believe that Amenhotep II was buried on a small mound, while his female priestess was buried on the other side of the tomb.
The Archaeology of Giza and other ancient Egyptian tombs
The ancient Egyptians believed in a mummy cult. These tombs were usually made of stone, mud, and a jasmine vine that was used to encase the mummies inside the burial chamber.
There were also tombs constructed for royalty, which were located in the vicinity of the Amenhotep II mummies’ tomb.
Due to their age and complexity, the tombs were considered important locations, where mummies could be protected from the elements.
According to a report by A. Nassib, the tomb has long been a focus of archaeologists and experts.
The team discovered an old doorway, covered by a layer of vines. The secret passage is located in a small, enclosed courtyard. They also found another entrance, which leads to the southeastern side of the tomb.
It is believed that the original entrance of the tomb was opened to the outside world by a giant fire. After that, the tomb was sealed, causing it to rot.
Ancient Egyptians built many temples. During the Ptolemaic period, a great religious movement developed in Egypt. While the city of Thebes was the center of the ancient civilization, other cities like Alexandria and Karnak also became known for their religious beliefs.
The German archaeologist Ludwig v. Bunning built a temple to Ptolemy, which is believed to be one of the oldest in the world. In 1864, Egyptologist Giovanni Battista Cassaddei found 50 tombs on the outskirts of the city.
It was believed that these tombs had undergone decades of desecration. The purpose of these tombs was believed to be the tomb of the deceased pharaoh or the temple they were buried in.
The location of these tombs was unimportant, and it is believed that the tombs were not dug for religious purposes.
It is also believed that a select few tombs were always in use. The knowledge of tombs is not something that many people understand.
Ancient tombs are filled with gold, turquoise, and metallic bronze, gems, and even papyrus scrolls. These tombs have an estimated value of over 1 million Egyptian pounds ($13 million).
The Egyptians believed in living after death. Their famous mummies are now considered priceless, having been mummified more than 3,500 years ago. The mummies, which are still alive, had been buried on a nearby island, as a result of the Egyptian catastrophe.
What to do with the Egyptian Mummies?
Since it is believed that Egyptians believed in the idea of “ascending to eternal life.” While they buried their dead in the ground and decompose into water and fire, they often turned the corpse into mummies, which were then buried in a tomb.
In 1864, more than 50 tombs were found, of which only 20 were excavated.
The researchers who carried out the excavation were led by George John Briennig.
The tombs were found in far-off places. Many tombs are believed to have been built on sacred mountains. These tombs were very popular, especially during the Ptolemaic period. It is believed that in the late 5th century B.C.E., the so-called Golden Age of Egypt, the country lost its hold on the entire Middle East.
Egypt’s political and cultural relevance decreased, which is attributed to the growing interests of the new Arab nations and the declining influence of the mighty Roman Empire.
Although some of the tombs were discovered to have been lost, the majority of them were hidden and left untouched.
Through the excavation process, many mysteries were revealed. The experts have been able to discern the types of tools used by the people who built these tombs.
Ancient Egyptian Mummies
The Egyptians were skilled in engineering and architecture. It is believed that most tombs were built using the same techniques.
It was believed that the Egyptians were buried in large tombs, with a servant helping the deceased to the back. The entire process was completed using special mortars that were required for the tomb.
After the death of the deceased, the tombs were covered by a thick wall. After the wall was constructed, the tombs were covered with a layer of colored mud.
It is believed that the quality of the tomb was decided by the number of coffins and mummies inside the tomb.
More than 3,000 mummies were discovered in the tomb, and they had been relocated to other tombs.
Many researchers were attracted to the tombs. They were able to discover ancient cults that people used. It was believed that these cults were related to the belief of eternal life after death.
The purpose of the discovery was to be able to create a tomb of the dead that would not decay, making it eternal.
There is a lot to discover, and scientists will have to go back and read the ancient texts to understand the meaning of the artifacts.
Egypt’s Present
Egypt is located in North Africa, Northwest Asia, and the Red Sea area. The official languages are Arabic, French, English, and Russian.
Egypt has developed into a tourist destination with many tourists coming from different places. Most of the people come from around the world and are divided into different categories based on their needs.
According to the report published by Egypt Today, the number of people who visit Egypt in 2019 was around 3.5 million. The number of people who visit Egypt annually is around 10 million.

At dawn, the mountains cast shadows that seemed to dominate the sky, creating a magnificent scene that looked faraway. In a calm and quiet atmosphere, looking back to look over my shoulder, I saw the iconic peak of Mount Fuji, one of Japan’s most representative mountains, gleaming in the moonlight, a 3,792-meter high tip that should not be missed in any itinerary around Japan.
Fueled by an early morning breakfast and the energy of the mountain, I left the hotel at 6:30 a.m. After a 20-minute drive, we entered Mount Fuji’s Monasana Hakuenai-jin station, which looked like a quiet and well-kept town with an abundance of shops and restaurants, while we all took off our shoes and entered the station’s entrance.
Upon checking in, we headed straight to the signboard, waiting for the train to depart. On the narrow train tracks, I felt that life was in good hands as we waited for the blossoming cherry trees along the route.
We arrived at the beginning of the route, to be greeted by a unique mosaic made of cherry blossoms that shone with red and pink blooms, and then immersed in nature. The serene environment, along with the sound of the blossoming trees, gave us the sense of being in the forest.
It seemed that we had almost been running from the airport to the Monasana Hakuenai-jin station, a little on the edge of town and with no people, but it felt like we had travelled to another world, as we entered a calming landscape.
We finally left the city and, just after 8:00 a.m., arrived at the Fuji 5 station, where we changed into our own clothes and put on our hats. As we prepared for the ascent, we all felt the mountain looming behind us, creating a calming sensation.
There was a light jacket around our waists and a hat in our hands, and while being a little gusty, we walked along the mountain tracks through lush green pine trees, waking up the natural environment, and heading straight up to the top of Mount Fuji.
Looking at the sea of clouds that were hiding at an altitude of 19,000 meters, it felt as if the clouds were just floating in the middle of a blue sea. The viewing platform on top was occupied by a group of people who had made a beautiful ceremony.
When the sun rose, it was indeed a scene of breathtaking beauty as we stood on the Fuji 5 Station’s viewing platform. We felt that the moment had arrived when we had reached the top of Mount Fuji, and that was also when we finally felt the experience of being in Japan, so we walked to the top of the mountain to enjoy the panoramic views.
Although we thought it was not high season, it was still an amazing day in Hakone, especially as we were able to enjoy the fresh air that fell through the trees along the mountainside.
After finishing up, we had a bit of a leisurely walk back to the hotel, which felt a bit like a pleasant summer afternoon in Hakone’s countryside.
At the base of Mount Fuji, there was a restaurant and a souvenir shop at the top of the hill, called “Onigiri”—the latter literally means fresh rice and a type of food from a traditional Japanese dish that includes meat, raw vegetables, and rice.
You can experience the traditional cuisine at the mountain restaurant, “Onigiri,” which was almost an outdoor café that embodied a sense of freedom and a joyful atmosphere, where you can be surrounded by nature without having to be too far from the city center.
The main courses of the meal included fresh pork, various kinds of nigiri (rice balls), egg dishes, and “Itako,” which are seafood dishes with dashi, which consists of a budo (herb-soaked rice, safflower), pickles, and seabass, and is also a common meal in Japan.
In addition to the meals at “Onigiri,” there were also several restaurants at the base of Mount Fuji that were offering meals and drinks, and a café with a view that was the perfect location to enjoy the stunning sunset.
After finishing up, we ended up not eating very much at “Onigiri,” but instead got into a 12-kilometer-long hiking trail, called “Fuji Trail,” by taking a taxi back to the city center.
The trail also gave a beautiful view of the city, with blossoming cherry trees at the top, which provided a delightful contrast between green and red, and after finishing it, we walked around the city’s city gates, which once again gave us that calm and peaceful sensation, as if we had entered a temple where we had been taken to a heavenly paradise.
It was at this moment that we saw the body of two Russian-Japanese men who had collapsed in front of Mount Fuji. Although the situation was unfortunate, it seemed that they had already received the best of fortune as the sun was setting, with lush greenery and a perfect light.
I began thinking about the many people who have died while climbing in the mountains, as if they were preparing for a great feast of happiness, and it was as if it was about to happen.

The young inventor's new device promised to revolutionize the relationship between machines and humans
Tuesday November 13 2017
The world of 3D printing continues to improve, and there are still improvements to be made. The latest development in this revolution is the ability of a device known as the 3D Mimicking Bio-robot, to control digital 3D models of bacteria in the lungs of a human to perform an internal examination. The 3D Mimicking Bio-robot, which was developed by the 3D University, is currently being tested in an experimental phase and could improve many kinds of non-invasive surgical procedures.
Like many 3D printing projects, this 3D Mimicking Bio-robot is a machine based on a lot of plastic. The 3D Mimicking Bio-robot itself is made of an iron oxide and acrylic mixture, which is able to reproduce human cells' complex tissues and organs without the need of a bone marrow, fetal brain, nerve and even a vein.
Inside of the robot, a box of micro-parts called "protoplanes" is placed to allow their genetic information to be transcribed into the desired cells, and to verify the growth of cells. In fact, this box of protoplanes is what allows for the movement of cells to reach the desired location, while the robot uses force to make sure cells in uninhabitable areas are not pushed. In addition, the prototype was modified to have LEDs inside the box, so the 3D Mimicking Bio-robot could be lit in dark areas, such as where blood has been cut off, by injecting the black plastic box with a light source.
However, despite all of these benefits, the robot is still in the experimental phase and the team still has many things to improve, such as that the robot has to be more precise and has to be able to be more precise than 100 millimetres. In this case, the problems are very similar to the problems in 3D printers, although in this case, the robot does not only transmit digital information, but also physical information. The robot is designed to replace the metal grid on the front of the chest, which allows it to track the internal organs and the inside of the body. This means that, for example, when the robot gets into contact with the heart, it can be able to perform various types of heart tests, using the built-in multimodal sensors.
While the robot can be programmed to move in certain directions and perform tasks, the robot cannot perform any jobs that involve moving parts larger than 15 millimetres, and this is why the 3D Mimicking Bio-robot is designed to be controlled by human assistance. The project is currently underway, and is aiming to create a small version of the robot to be used in medicine.

The mysterious stranger in town had a story that made people run.
A train in the snow passed through, the guy in the trolley told the woman behind the counter: If the train was moving, he couldn’t help you.
The woman had given the man the identity of a guide.
The woman had even given him a gun.
A year later, two strangers would come to meet at a village inn to talk about the woman they had met, and to tell their stories.
The first story was the one that was told to me.
I met an old friend of mine.
We had both lived in this tiny hamlet deep in Newfoundland. We knew we had to talk soon.
After a few days, he knocked on my door.
“Mister Tim,” he said.
“Can I borrow your car?” I asked.
“No, I’ve just the old farmhouse, I can’t rent it.” The man had a house and a yard. “The town is really small. Your car would get stuck if you tried to leave without me driving it, so here it is for you.” He gave me his keys and I got behind the wheel. He turned the car’s lights on and off as he sped down the road.
I didn’t see the man again after that, but as I walked away from town, I wondered if I had made a real friend in this quiet village.
The second story was the one I knew best.
That story belonged to a writer named John Fleming, who lived in Carmenfield, Alberta. The woman he met in his story was called Alice.
When I met her I didn’t know how to ask her about herself. When I finally did, the stories became my focus. I began to write about them and sometimes to go and see them in the village.
I had a couple of friends in town who asked me what I thought of their friend Alice, and I knew I had to tell them the stories.
I told them about her unusual lover, John Spencer, who refused to change his nature. I told them how she treated him like his whole life. They listened to the stories, and as I continued I discovered that the men in the stories had an unusual connection with Alice, and with their unusual stories she told them were theirs to tell.
And then one day I found myself driving my new friend’s car around town.
He hadn’t mentioned me once, so I figured he had forgotten about me. When I finally got home, his car was parked near the village hall.
“How was it?” I asked.
He shook his head and said “It’s too late. It’s too late.” I sighed and told him I was going to go and find the old woman I had met with a year earlier.
It was going to be a long, long drive. I had to change and get ready. It would be early morning by the time I got home.
I asked my old friend if he had brought me an antique tea light he had brought in from Newfoundland, but the old man said, “No, I never brought anything in.”
As I drove through town I couldn’t help but notice all the people in the storefronts, the tiny shops, the houses.
I went inside the old woman’s house. It was completely secluded. All the things in the house were theirs, and the things they owned, and they were all filled with boxes.
“How can I live here,” I asked. “How do you make it?”
“You don’t need to know that,” the woman replied.
I found a pile of boxes next to her.
I opened one of the boxes, and I found an antique tea light that I had not noticed before. Inside it was packed and unpacked and wrapped in green wool. It was hard to understand what the old woman was looking for. But when I opened the tea light, I saw the word that had been sewn in.
“Can you help me, Mr. Wood?” she said.
I stared at the tea light, at its soft glow.
Then the woman explained to me the story of her special person, her extraordinary story.
But then, for a moment, I wondered if I had made a friend in this small village.

Trees and grains among my favorite subjects in photography.
If your home has walls for porches, they're sometimes built with large, unfinished windows that present an interesting and recognizable profile for the homeowner to show visitors. They're also good for baking bread; a laundry basket of towels is common.
But sometimes we want to change the view of our home, so we add a door to the porch, or install a deck or patio. Doing so changes the look of the home, but we know this decorative trick affects the natural balance and harmony of a home. As a result, we seek new ways to make our homes more comfortable for our inhabitants.
The easy answer is to paint walls, but this is a bit of a cheat. It has to look like it's a solid wall, even if it's a painted wall. It doesn't help that most walls are plastered, covered with tiles, or carved from brick. Because of its consistency, it can be hard to cut a perfectly straight line from one wall to the next.
Other cheats are to add other types of exterior coverings, such as a screen door. It may look like your home has an underground swimming pool, but the underground pool has a tiled surface and doesn't seem very natural.
So what do you do to make your home's existing design more balanced?
Grow roots
If you plant new shrubs and flowers, and especially if you use multiple types of shrubs and flowers, you'll add an interesting layer to the garden. The colors you plant help to accentuate natural borders that make it seem as if you've grown something inside. But even if you just keep a few plants, you'll have a stronger sense of cohesion in the garden.
Of course, you have to know how to grow shrubs and flowers. If you're worried about how the tree will grow, see if there's a safe spot to place the root ball. Here you can plant all kinds of root balls.
Alternatively, use a rotting tree to enhance the look of your yard. To maintain this type of shrub, you'll need to plant different varieties of shrubs and trees at varying levels. They'll give the yard an airy look and become layered against the grass.
The best trees and shrubs for the garden are bare root shrubs that show off their roots.
Little "boxes" of shrubs or trees can be created by inserting a pair of plastic pipe sections into existing holes. This technique looks like a garden for the birds, and it also allows you to move shrubs and trees from one location to another, without taking up too much space.
Of course, you'll want to make sure you do this the right way.
Insulating the walls
What you don't want is thick walls for a house with floors that run out to the street. Weight gain from a wall leads to the loss of that weight. It's true that walls help create insulation, but if you use just enough of them, the warmth will still get through.
If you're going to put a wall up, make sure it doesn't offer too much structural resistance. The right amount is a function of the type of material and the area of the wall. Look at the joints on the edge of a wall, and especially at the location where one wall meets the other. You can do this with a trowel.
Perhaps it's time to install energy-saving insulation in your walls. New solar panels can provide light and heat for an area, and your insulation isn't that bad to look at. You can even be as simple as topping it with wool or insulation foam.
Create an inexpensive planter
In the winter, flowers are in their prime and these make a nice addition to the planting. By placing an abundance of bright yellow or pink flowers at the foot of a wall in your garden, they'll make the garden look more spacious. Even better, you can reuse this display: a planter can be added to the back of a hanging basket.
This arrangement doesn't have a problem with rain. It can also be moved on a stand, making it easy to place in a corner of the garden. Use this planter for a lot of natural floral arrangements or small, but interesting, potted plants. And don't forget about all those water lilies.
Wall color
Painting the exterior walls of a home is a great way to add a splash of color. Think of the color used to paint the shutters and doors. But once the main color is applied, it's tough to change it without some serious damage to the interior walls.
You could sand the exterior of the walls and it will look better. However, that can cause interior damage. Once you've settled on the color of the exterior walls, use a paint sprayer and apply two coats of paint to the inside. Use a thin layer of primer on the interior of the home to further soak up any damage.
If you want to do this a DIY project, use an epoxy primer on the outside and then a thin coat of paint on the inside. That way, you can choose which coat you want to use, or which one will offer you the best results.

The lone hiker's journey across the desert tested the limits of her resilience.
by Heather Cladwell | October 29, 2018
Travel is amazing! But it can also be quite scary, especially when you’re the lone hiker for a three-day trek.
But that’s where I’m going to take off from my most recent adventure, this weekend when I’ll hike 24 miles from the Sunset Crater Visitor Center to the summit of the 2,112-foot granite peak in the Cinder cone of the Joshua Tree National Park. On top of that, I will be the only female hiker through the entire trek, taking on the challenge of carrying 52 pounds of gear, navigating 500-foot switchbacks, and slogging through 1,500-foot swamps, sand dunes, and massive washes.
“I just feel invincible,” says Heather Stone, a Carlsbad, Calif.-based spokeswoman for Amber Alert. “It’s kind of like riding a wave. You can catch it and then get up on it again.”
She found it just as she did.
Stone traveled to Joshua Tree with a trio of 15-year-old girls. The three-day trip is a program designed for girls ages 12 to 14 to experience outdoors by increasing their understanding of the environment, helping build self-confidence, developing leadership skills, and establishing healthy lifestyles.
The girls, in turn, shared with Stone their expectations and hopes for the trek. And they asked her a very thought-provoking question.
“What do you expect this to be like?” Stone asked them.
The girls, who range in age from 14 to 18, didn’t blink. They all had visions of how to prepare for the trek. One looked into her backpack. Another looked into hers. Some had each other’s backs. They had their plastic shoes but didn’t wear them. One had some cooking gear and a sleeping bag, but didn’t want to risk walking barefoot across the desert floor.
“What I expect it to be like is a lot like living life on your own,” Stone says. “Everybody has a vision.
“Some people are going to be really fit and, like, ‘I’ve got to do it right now,’ and some people are just, ‘I’ll do it.’ And I think you’ll see how different the girls are. Some might be like, ‘No, I’ll do it,’ and some might be like, ‘I’ll make it work.’”
At the age of 15, both of the girls are taking advantage of the program’s limited enrollment and want to spend a full day hiking with the experienced staff. But most of all, they are overwhelmed with excitement and anticipation for what will be a challenging, but rewarding adventure.
“There are different levels of encouragement for the girls,” Stone says. “Some girls are, like, ‘I want to do this.’ And some girls are, like, ‘I’m just gonna follow behind the girls.’ ”
During the first day of the trip, Stone led the girls from the main parking lot to their vehicles. As they returned to their vehicles to begin the hike, one girl stepped on a fallen rock and her knee started to swell. Another needed some help assembling a tent.
“It took me back to my 12-year-old self,” Stone says. “I remember it so clearly, so vividly. It’s been 12 years since I experienced something like that.”
One of the girls’ mothers, Ellie, led the other girls through a hard, sandy wash where they had to walk the thin wooden sticks that the girls would be carrying through the thick tumbleweed and swamp.
“They came all the way back here from Mission Basin to help me walk through the thing that makes my heart ache,” Ellie says.
“I had to look for a rock,” Stone says. “I’m not even trying to make this stuff up. I was just looking for something solid underneath.”
“I think I’m gonna fall down and stay down,” Ellie says.
Eventually, Ellie finished with her girls and they returned to the car lot. As the sun started to set, they left and began the long descent back to their vehicles.
After their return trip, the girls told Stone they had enjoyed the first day.
“I don’t know if I ever want to do this again, but that was fun,” Ellie says. “I learned a lot of new things.”
One girl in particular was excited for a new challenge.
“I felt like I could use it,” says Jessica McCarthy. “I was exhausted, but I didn’t want to stop. I was having so much fun.”
“I really enjoyed every second of it,” Ellie says.
It’s taken 41 days to reach the summit of Cinder. On the third and final day of the hike, the group reached the trailhead. They made the 10-mile descent to the base of the climb. The girls were pleased to find their water back. The girls, who had only carried one gallon backpacks, each found a 5-gallon jug and carted it back to the car, plus the rope they had just pulled across the floor of a cavern. The girls will return the water to the base of the climb during the following days.
“They were like, ‘Oh, my goodness, I’m so close to the top,’ ” Ellie says.
“It’s so hard to say, but I just think the girls enjoyed it. I loved it,” Stone says.
“It was my first time hiking up to the crater and seeing the huge granite boulders.”
During her trip, Stone was struck by the beauty of the Joshua Tree’s landscape and by her new friendships.
“I realized that I wanted to do more like this,” she says. “I started looking around the world for the next big challenge.”
To learn more about the girls’ newfound friendship, read Stone’s memoir, “Let’s Make the Road,” on the Amber Alert website.
This story was provided to the Banner by Heather Cladwell, a Carlsbad, Calif., spokeswoman for Amber Alert.

During a board game night that becomes reality, players find themselves in a life-sized game of Poker at their local casino. The tables turn and cards are face up, but each player is trying to decide who the “three-of-a-kind” have been dealt.
The winner is determined at random, and unbeknownst to the players, the third card could be revealing information that could have led the winner to have an advantage in the future.
Among the players is bartender Daniel, who is sure that he knows the right card, but is unsure if he’s the one to deal. Despite his uncertainty, he plays the game, and with no blind bet and no fixed result, he tries to gather information from the card.
One of the players, Ellen, is also a casino employee and fan of blackjack. She finds herself trying to find out who the “three-of-a-kind” are in order to beat the dealer. She plays the game, and even though she’s the one in the largest stake, she’s pretty sure she is the only one who knows what her playing partner is actually doing, as she never saw the cards before.
The last player, Oscar, is a beer brewer by trade, but he’s a charter member of the Blackjack Club. He makes his way to the top table with the players, but then he gets dealt the three-of-a-kind card, and in an effort to beat the dealer, he is compelled to take out the huge chip. He plays the game, and this time, he wants to avoid the three-of-a-kind, because he doesn’t want to miss the opportunity to strike a winning bet.
When the game begins, all cards are dealt face-up and players aren’t allowed to look at their hands before they bet. Players begin placing their bets, and the first player to reach the 50/50 bet amount wins. All players must wager at least 50 units of money, and if the players find the three-of-a-kind that they dealt when they are playing, the player must lose the 100.
The best way to win in Poker, says the director of the film, is to play the game with good luck and by paying attention to the players. The film’s description makes it clear that the film is an inspection of the value of blackjack, and blackjack is not to be the game for the gambler.
Players and casinos have a lot in common. They provide social interaction, entertainment, and opportunities to gamble. The biggest differences between the two, however, are that blackjack is played with a count, and the value of the cards is added to the stakes. The difference is significant.
In blackjack, the stakes are quite high. If the player’s chip value is too low, then he or she can either give up and play with the next card, or they can bet to the bank or to the table with the players in it. A high stake gives the players a sense of danger.
In blackjack, the players can change their bets at any time, and they do so often. Players can’t pay attention to the stakes, and they will bet more than they should.
In the game, the players have a variety of advantages, such as a small prize pool for the winners, an opportunity to play for free, and an opportunity to play for cash prizes. The casinos also enjoy the rush of the experience. Players enjoy knowing that they are playing a game with the best of the best, and that they could be in for a big win.

Drifting through the cosmos, the comet harbors the ability to display the mysteries of the universe for the rest of its time. We want to know more about its components and composition; no such questions are possible without knowing how the comet was formed.
Our molecular clock measures from the Sun.
The comet’s surface shows a track of radiation as a result of leaving the inner solar system. The bright solar spot is converted into a comet mark, and its path is traced in the comet’s orbit.
The comet’s surface is icy and the bulk of the comet is covered by ice. A squeeze of material brings water to the surface; the water forms stains and circles on the comet. Water is frozen and cools into droplets.
The core is formed in the same way as the comet’s outer shell. The comet is susceptible to explosions from the core collapsing and causing a shock wave to the surrounding space. The shock wave forms a pressure pump that works to raise the temperature of the frozen interior. Ice is lowered to a temperature of 277 degrees Kelvin. Comets are stable to heat and may pass the sun, but they do not increase the temperature of the comet.
The ionosphere is a vortex, where hydrogen and other ions move in an electrically charged state. On the surface of the comet, the ions and the hydrogen shell are charged to give rise to electric fields that push the ions into opposite directions.
Nature breaks the electromagnetic radiation down into a ghostly radio wave. The ghostly radio wave transforms into electromagnetic radiation that is less violent and keeps the energy within the field around the comet intact.
The comet contains up to 500 volatile substances, including ammonia, methane, methane sulfide, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water. Atmospheric gases are primarily from these substances, the composition of which matches the presence of specific substances on the surface of the comet. Scientists have therefore hypothesized that the comet is primarily formed from volatile materials.
In this work, we examine the materials that can compose the comet. We see that the comet has a white color and a blue hue, from their polarity to their pH. The volatiles have been tracked and some of them have been measured.

The skate park, as it’s called, opened its doors in 2019 to a largely local community looking to do something that was needed at the time: give back to the city. Bettendorf, as I was later to learn, is home to the Black Car Industrial Park, one of four railroad car yards in the state of Iowa. The industrial park itself covers 26 acres of railroad land and makes up 30 percent of Bettendorf’s industrial base. The yards were closed to the public after industrial companies like Norfolk Southern shut them down to comply with COVID-19 health standards. Black Car Line, an effort of the local community, was the only way to get the facilities back up and running again.
This adventure was planned months in advance, and as an avid skateboarder, my trek to Bettendorf was not short on exercise. Wearing a mask at all times, I plunked down about $150 to rent the park. So, I’ve been back again, a few times now, over the last couple of years, to explore what’s left of Bettendorf. The park is named after a restored Old Orchard Mill on the property, built by the late Daniel Alexander Buchanan in 1850, a world-renowned inventor in the industrial age, born in Bettendorf. The man whose product was a light bulb made the town his home, before moving his family to the newly established city.
A glimpse of the Bettendorf skate park
As a newcomer to the skate park, I had no idea what I was in for. Sure, there were giant ramps with long rails, and long ledges for small boarders, but it didn’t feel right. This may have been a twinge of impatience as my friends had suggested to me to try the newly constructed dog park.
Over the next few months, I slowly learned the art of sneaking away to check out the skate park at different times of the day, when it was at its busiest. I would take the day off work, and leave the office behind at the wrong hours.
Although some were unsure of whether I’d return, it wasn’t long before I began to pick up a small community in Bettendorf again. I was practically run off by others who came to the park and learned how to skateboard on it. I stuck to that small community, and it got me really excited about the skate park. By January 2021, I was relocating from California to Bettendorf to finish my work and was excited to see what lay ahead.
Once I began to hear about the skate park back in Bettendorf, I began to imagine a secret garden that I hadn’t known existed in town. I started to feel like there was something waiting for me when I visited the skate park.
Much to my surprise, Black Car Line just made it easier to explore. The park hosts rangers to meet the visitors, and various public and private events are held throughout the year.
As I returned to the skate park, I remembered the time I started to feel a bit lost, when I asked if there was anything special about the skate park.
“We have to welcome everyone,” said Bob, the park ranger. “That is one of the things we are here for. A lot of people want to learn about it. A lot of people want to do it, but also want to have fun and meet new people.”
It was a warm summer day, and so I continued to discover a new secret garden that I hadn’t yet seen at the skate park. I went off the ranger’s path and walked toward a single ramp.
Almost immediately, I was overcome with disbelief. Just off the main ramp were a few decks, with regular flat rails and grinding boxes and pumps. I looked around for another skate park, but there were no park managers, no information boards, and I wasn’t quite sure if there was anything there.
I then saw the main ramp as I approached. The entire ramp was adorned with wooden slats that the park managers had built up to create a platform, meant for a bowl. A new addition, but more steep than I had ever seen before.
The beach-like ramp would have been perfect for a park manager, and led to the best bowl in town.
On the ramp

A stunning bowl in a secret garden
There were some other small decks and a few ramps here and there. I watched the ranger walk up and down the large ramp with someone.
“I don’t know,” I thought to myself, not sure how I wanted to begin to explore.
“Be careful,” I thought to myself, remembering the time I almost fell to my death over the last time I visited.
As I walked further into the hidden garden, I made my way around the ramp and went down to the surface of the cliff. The ramp was very steep, and I saw other people with no problem on their backs, walking up and down the slope without care, so I knew I was taking a mistake.
Tucked into the deep part of the garden, I walked around the perimeter until I was alone. I pushed my way into the path of that small box, and, low and silent, I practically came to a stop as I stood on the edge.
Another large group was having a party on the park land. I made a little noise, and they all screamed at me to get back. I immediately retreated into the box, and then went back into the garden as I knew I couldn’t go back there.
I didn’t want to just sit there, so I started to walk around and check the hidden parts of the park. At the bottom of the large grassy hill, there were lots of stones, small piles of earth and small hills in the middle of the grounds. An isolated area in the park

The beach-like wall of gravel

The concrete structure with wires

Concrete bowl with wires inside

A different kind of island in the park

Wet grassy island

A cricket on grass in a hidden garden

I continued to walk through the bowl, just feeling like I wanted to wash it. Finally, I walked over and onto the rock.
I was completely drenched, in a park no longer. I let the water drip down the rock, but I was stuck there.
“I don’t know,” I said to myself as I let the water drip.

A tree that once grew above the water pond, but is now rotting

In the distance, I could see the redoubtable boulder in the park. I began to think of how to get home, and wanted to get out of there as soon as possible.
The tree roots in the rock’s base had broken off, and the branches were on the side of the rock.

A green area, but mostly dried up

From here, the rock to the platform looked nothing like the rest of the park. The rocks were perfectly smooth, much harder than the rest of the rock I’d seen in the park. I found the idea very odd, but I moved on.
Near a set of stairs

The only other black leaves were on the rock
